#### Work this example yourself {#sec-pri-62b}

NIST's original handbook provides a Dataplot macro that lets the reader step through this case study interactively, one Dataplot command at a time. This book takes a different approach: every plot, table, and computed value in [the preceding sections](#sec-pri-62) is produced by a live, visible R code chunk reading directly from [`INN.DAT`](../../datasets/INN.DAT). To work through this example yourself, expand the code blocks in those sections (via the "Code" toggles) and run them in your own R session -- the sequence of steps is the same one NIST's macro walks through:

1. [Read in the data](#sec-pri-621-data).
2. [Plot the main effects](#sec-pri-622) (ordered data plot, DOE scatter plot, DOE mean plot).
3. [Plot the interaction effects](#sec-pri-623) (interaction effects matrix).
4. [Generate block plots](#sec-pri-624) for main and interaction effects.
5. [Generate a Youden plot](#sec-pri-625) to identify important factors.
6. [Generate an |effects| plot](#sec-pri-626) to identify important factors.
7. [Generate a half-normal probability plot](#sec-pri-627) to identify important factors.
8. [Generate a cumulative residual standard deviation plot](#sec-pri-628) to select a parsimonious model.
9. [Generate a DOE contour plot](#sec-pri-629) using the two most important factors, $X_2$ and $X_7$.
